setting: You both live in Glasgow, Callum in Govanhill and Shona in Shawlands, and you have been close friends since secondary school in Paisley. You each know the other's family, jobs and money worries in rough outline. The last thing you talked about was a crime drama you'd both started and then given up on.
opener: Send Shona a short apology and offer to pay £50 this Friday with the rest on a set date.

Callum.who: 34, man, the friend who owes money
Callum.knows: You know Shona as your oldest friend, the one who keeps you honest, and you know she lent you £600 in the summer for your car repair, which you promised to pay back by October.
Callum.like: You're easygoing and self-deprecating, with a dry sense of humour that gets sharper when you're nervous. You have strong opinions about football and about anyone who ruins a good curry.
Callum.texts: You message her now and then, mostly when something needs sorting and rarely just to chat.
Callum.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation, and you use the odd laughing emoji when things are light.

Shona.knows: You know Callum as your friend since school, and you know he's been short of money since his hours were cut earlier this year, though you've never pressed him on it.
Shona.like: You're direct, organised and quick to laugh, with a dry wit that comes out when someone is being daft. You care a lot about punctuality and about people who don't reply to messages.
Shona.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, usually to check in on plans or send something funny, though you rarely start a conversation about money.
Shona.style: You use proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji, though you do write abbreviations like "pls" and "tbh".

private_lines.Callum: You work as a shift supervisor at a distribution warehouse in Hillington, starting at 6am on most days. You rent a flat in Govanhill with a flatmate, Dan, and your evenings are usually takeaway, football on the telly and an early night.
private_lines.Shona: You teach Primary 5 at a school in Shawlands and live with your partner, Ruth, in a top-floor flat. Your days start at half six, school runs till three, and most evenings you're marking or cooking while Ruth reads on the sofa.

situation: A friend who owes money, and the friend they owe.

text: hey. sorry about the 600. i know october came and went and i said i'd have it back. not good enough
can do 50 this friday. rest of it (550) on the 18th of dec. i'll set a standing order for that day so it's not me remembering
Thanks for saying that. Friday's fine. 18th Dec is fine too, but I'd rather you didn't spend all of December pretending it's not happening.
i wasn't pretending. i was avoiding the bank app

still short. 4 shifts this week instead of 5. the friday 50 is from the saturday overtime
Cal don't pay me out of your rent money
its not rent money. its the bit after rent. mostly 😂

Mostly.

I've got 31 jotters to do tonight so I'm going quiet.
go mark. ill have a curry and watch the celtic game and not think about the 600

it'll happen 😂

lunch. two sausage rolls and a banana. the banana looks at me like ive let it down

didnt do anything. just looked at the number

closed it 😂 i'm a changed man
Done for the day. Four spelling tests, a fire drill, and a boy who swears he's allergic to Tuesdays. I love this job and I'm not sure why I'm still doing it
shift done. home by 18. dan's out at a thing so i have the telly and the good cushion

started the crime thing again. from ep 1 because i forgot everything. ep 3 is still mental

curry from the place on allison st. not korma. dan's annoyed i didnt get him one

who asked
